previous_versions.body: @randomstuff could you do me a favour and suggest a simple PR to address these issues? I don't think we want to start messing with the requirements here too much but mostly focus on clarity and dealing with terminology.
@randomstuff could you do me a favour and suggest a simple PR to address these issues?

> 17.2.1 Verify that the key for the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) certificate is private by ensuring it is not reused in existing products or open-source projects and confirming it is not distributed or leaked.

Proving that the private key is not leaked is not possible but we can verify that the key is not hardcoded in the application at the very least.

> Are the secure cipher suites the same as regular TLS?

Yes, the ciphersuites are shared with TLS and we can use the same list (or criterions) of allowed ciphersuites.

> Is there a central source of truth for of secure protection profiles?

There are guidelines such as:

* [ciphersuite.info](https://ciphersuite.info/)
* [Mozilla SSL Configuration Generator](https://ssl-config.mozilla.org/)

And we have list of allowed encryption methods, MACs, hashing methods in the appendix and the reader can derive a list of allowed ciphersuites from that. I'm not sure I want to maintain a list of ciphersuites (dans SRTP protection profiles) in the appendix however. Ideally we could derive it from the list of underlying approved cryptographic mechanisms using a script.
